source: X API public reads (get_users_posts) on 11 Nov 2026. Official accounts: original posts since 1 Oct 2026. @elonmusk and @nextbigfuture: company-relevant posts only (SpaceX, Starlink, Starship, SPCX, Starmind, Grok/SI). Short off-topic replies were omitted. created_at is the original X timestamp (UTC).
missing: No public official X account found for CFO Bret W. Johnsen (checked 11 Nov 2026).
@xai now redirects in bio to @SpaceXSI; @SpaceXAI was not a live handle.
@grok is a very high-volume product account and is linked from the page rather than fully ingested.

posts.name: Brian Wang
posts.text:
Grok Bot 1.0  is a massive upgrade as they all work together and take initiative automatically $SPCX 

Grok Bot team automatically collaborate with each other, take initiative, and continuously improve  

Here's what's NEW:  

1. MULTIPLAYER TEAMMATES

posts.summary: Brian Wang calls Grok Bot 1.0 a massive upgrade for $SPCX, saying the bots now work together, take initiative automatically and continuously improve, quoting an XFreeze post on SpaceXSI’s official 1.0 launch. He lists new multiplayer teammate features (sharing bots, Slack and Microsoft Teams, and video meetings), proactive monitoring and follow-up, team-wide learning, and stronger browser, document and integration tools, arguing the biggest shift is that bots no longer need every task assigned.

posts.text:

posts.summary: Brian Wang says SpaceX’s Colossus 2 AI data-center campus has bought new southwest property known as Project Mitchell and is getting approval for more power, which he sees as likely a new AI data center beyond the five already being built or near completion. An accompanying map labels Project Mitchell on the southwest side of a Colossus 2 campus that includes Macrohard buildings, and he adds that SpaceX has started buying nearby southeast homes, which he says would likely reduce power-plant noise issues, after SpaceXSI’s 1.2 GW Mississippi permit win.

posts.name: Brian Wang
posts.text: $SPCX gets  Mississippi 1.2 Gigawatt air permit https://t.co/Qw2LvkAduV
posts.summary: Brian Wang notes that SPCX has received a 1.2 gigawatt air permit in Mississippi, quoting an XFreeze post about the same decision. That post says Mississippi’s Environmental Quality Permit Board voted on 10 November to uphold the air permit for SpaceXSI’s permanent Southaven power plant after two days of testimony.

posts.name: Brian Wang
posts.text: $TSLA and maybe $SPCX might move HQ to Florida. https://t.co/KWzqvQIHe4
posts.summary: Brian Wang writes that Tesla, and maybe SpaceX, might move their headquarters to Florida, quoting a post that says Governor Ron DeSantis has invited Musk to relocate Tesla’s HQ from Texas. The quoted post is commentary about a political invitation after Democrats won in Texas, not a SpaceX or Tesla announcement that a move is happening.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.summary: Musk replies that 100 GW in space is roughly equal to 800 GW on Earth, arguing the two are not the same at all. He adds that terrestrial solar must be paired with massive batteries to keep compute running at night and supplemented with combustion or nuclear power in winter.

posts.name: Starlink
posts.text:
Home in rural Oklahoma is where this veteran and his wife enjoy the things that matter most.

With Starlink, they can stream, study, and stay connected with family and friends, reliably and seamlessly.

Discover their story this Veterans Day. https://t.co/dJDhgku0iK
posts.summary: Starlink posted a Veterans Day customer video featuring Marine veteran John Hassell and nursing student Ashley Hassell, who live on five acres about an hour southwest of Oklahoma City. They say they use the service for VA telehealth, Ashley’s online nursing degree, streaming, gaming and family video calls, and that coverage held up during recent tornado warnings; it is a marketing testimonial, not a new product or plan announcement.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
@IterIntellectus Actually, we’re aiming for 1TW/year from Earth, rising to over 1PW/year from the Moon. 

That’s why I say that if we achieve this outcome, SpaceX will obviously be worth more than Earth, because space is so staggeringly enormous!
posts.summary: Musk replies that SpaceX is aiming for 1 TW of capacity a year from Earth, rising to over 1 PW a year from the Moon, in response to a post about the company’s 100 GW-per-year solar equipment order. He adds that if that outcome is achieved, SpaceX will “obviously be worth more than Earth, because space is so staggeringly enormous.”

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
@zerohedge SpaceX has a chance of going about half the GW next year of actually usable compute. 

“Actually usable” is an important metric. It takes us ~2 months working 24/7 to get a large compute cluster working reliably. I’d guess closer to 6 months for others.
posts.summary: Replying to a ZeroHedge post on how much of developers’ data-center pipelines actually gets built, Musk says SpaceX has a chance next year of delivering about half the gigawatts as “actually usable” compute. He stresses that “actually usable” matters, saying it takes SpaceX about two months of 24/7 work to get a large cluster running reliably, and he guesses closer to six months for others.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
@aaronburnett We would be happy to take the compute back. No problem.

But I think the opposite is going to happen.
posts.summary: Musk replies that SpaceX would be “happy to take the compute back. No problem,” but that he thinks “the opposite is going to happen,” in a thread about reports that Anthropic told sell-side analysts it may not extend a SpaceX compute contract beyond mid-next year. Those claims about contract size and revenue impact come from other posters in the thread, not from Musk or an official company statement.

posts.summary: Musk, asked about models, says Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 is “a masterpiece” but that Grok 5 “should exceed” it, perhaps in two or three months, with continued acceleration after that. That is a product-timeline comment from the CEO, not a dated backlog or revenue figure.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.summary: In a follow-up, Musk says the stack even includes some assembly, that superintelligence will one day write a better stack, and that the current code is “tight.” It continues the same thread about SpaceX rewriting its AI software in-house.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
@tetsuoai At SpaceX, we write our own headers and calculate our own time (includes leap seconds). Not many people will know what this means, but those that do will appreciate it.

The new Grok AI/SI training and inference stack is derived from incredible of work done by amazing engineers
posts.summary: Musk says SpaceX writes its own headers and calculates its own time (including leap seconds), and that the new Grok AI/SI training and inference stack comes from that engineering culture. For investors it underlines that Super Intelligence software is being built inside SpaceX, not only bought in.

posts.name: Elon Musk
posts.text:
@cradrrat We have dumped JAX/SGLang and rewritten the entire RL and inference stack from scratch in C/C++, which took some extra time. 

Training (aka pre-training) is done. Lot of cleanup was needed on the SFT data to get that mostly right. Now, 4.8 is in RL and the evals are starting to
posts.summary: Musk says the team has dumped JAX/SGLang and rewritten the reinforcement-learning and inference stack from scratch in C/C++, that pre-training is done, and that Grok 4.8 is now in RL with evals starting. This is a concrete update on the model-training schedule after a time-consuming rewrite.

- Delivered revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year-over-year

- Successfully launched our first revenue-generating Starship mission, delivering 26 Starlink V3 satellites to our broadband constellation, representing approximately 10x the downlink capacity added https://t.co/Qr94io6PiW
posts.summary: SpaceX’s Q3 highlights post states $14.6 billion of revenue, up 161% year over year, and the first revenue-generating Starship mission, which delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites with about 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch. Those figures match the official earnings release.

posts.text:

posts.name: Starlink
posts.text: In the last year, Starlink Mobile has connected more than 11 million people across @VEONGroup 3 key markets: Ukraine, Kazakhstan, and Bangladesh. posts.summary: Starlink says Starlink Mobile has connected more than 11 million people in a year across VEON’s Ukraine, Kazakhstan, and Bangladesh markets, often for messaging and location when cell towers cannot reach. A scale update for the direct-to-cell product in those countries.

posts.name: Starlink
posts.text: We have worked closely with regulators, industry and operators in India for 5+ years, and built a network of dedicated systems, gateways, and other infrastructure all in-country to exclusively serve Indian traffic safely and securely - and all with the requisite government https://t.co/zG8nqXW8WM
posts.summary: Starlink says it has worked with Indian regulators, industry, and operators for more than five years and has built in-country systems, gateways, and infrastructure so Indian traffic stays in India, “with the requisite government” approvals implied in the truncated post. It is a regulatory-and-infrastructure update on the India market, not a statement that consumer service is already fully live nationwide.

posts.summary: A thread follow-up says Grok Voice 3.0 hits frontier voice-agent performance at 40% lower latency and already resolves 70% of Starlink support calls on its own at SpaceX. That is a concrete cost-and-automation claim for the Connectivity support organisation.

posts.name: Starlink
posts.text: For those impacted by the earthquake in Panama, Starlink is providing free service through November 10 to new and existing customers in the affected areas. We are coordinating with emergency response agencies to help restore connectivity in the hardest-hit communities   →
posts.summary: Starlink is giving free service through 10 Nov to new and existing customers in areas of Panama affected by an earthquake, and says it is coordinating with emergency agencies. A disaster-relief offer, not a pricing change in other markets.

posts.text: Starlink Mobile is on a role!   Thank you ANATEL and @Baigorri1984 for approving Starlink Mobile’s priority spectrum rights to serve the  great people of Brazil. https://t.co/1HTFiwBhrj
posts.summary: Shotwell thanks Brazil’s ANATEL (and its then-head) for approving Starlink Mobile’s priority spectrum rights. It is official cheerleading for the same Brazilian spectrum decision described in the Starlink post.

posts.name: Starlink
posts.text:
ANATEL just scored a huge win for the people of Brazil by voting to approve Starlink Mobile's full 2 GHz access with our global S-band priority. 

Starlink will put this critical mid-band spectrum to work to make sure every Brazilian has access to high-speed mobile broadband on
posts.summary: Starlink says ANATEL voted to approve Starlink Mobile’s full 2 GHz access with global S-band priority, which the company says it will use for high-speed mobile broadband in Brazil. A key spectrum approval ahead of the later “now live with Vivo” announcement.

posts.name: Gwynne Shotwell
posts.text:
I have been a posting slug!

How about that launch triple header last week:  Starship, Crew 13, and Heavy!!!
Terrestrial low band spectrum acquisition and FCC approval for Starlink Mobile constellation!
And I am always relieved, grateful and proud when we complete a crew mission— https://t.co/YE3Ss1fdtD
posts.summary: Shotwell recaps a launch “triple header” — Starship, Crew-13, and Falcon Heavy — plus a terrestrial low-band spectrum acquisition and FCC approval for the Starlink Mobile constellation, and pride in completing a crew mission. A compact official summary of several operational and regulatory wins from that week.

posts.summary: Starlink will put its inflight service across American Airlines’ full mainline fleet so passengers can stream, game, work, and stay in touch. A large U.S. airline fleet win for the aviation vertical.
